input.question: why does renting a movie digitally cost so much more (usually 4-5 dollars) than renting a physical disc from a service like RedBox (usually 1-2 dollars)?
input.ground_truth: Simply a convenience fee. Also, movie companies charge a lot more for digital rights, as more people will stream/download them than buy the physical copy, that's why Netflix's physical library is much larger than their digital library.

Okay, let’s imagine you want to watch a fun cartoon.

If you rent the movie **digitally**, it’s like asking someone to bring the movie right to your TV or tablet over the internet. This costs more because the movie comes to you super fast, any time you want, and you don’t have to worry about giving it back or losing it. But the company that owns the movie has to pay for the special internet magic that brings it to you.

If you rent a **DVD from RedBox**, it’s like going to a little box outside and putting in a coin to get a disc. The company only has to worry about making and keeping those little boxes and discs. That’s cheaper for them, so they can charge you less.

So, digital renting costs more because it’s fancier and easier, but also a bit more expensive for the company to do!
